record: HOLDOUT_V3_PROBLEMS/1.0.0 (author: builder-r20s1, owner-delegated per AM24 D3; problems ONLY — the PRIVATE rubric is the auditor's instrument and is NEVER authored, seen, or assumed by the author)

problems.device: induced-draft cooling tower serving a hospital chilled-water plant, with film-fill packing and a basin
problems.failure: Legionella pneumophila colonizes the warm basin and film fill; quarterly sampling returns >1000 CFU/L, forcing shutdown-and-shock protocols that interrupt hospital cooling
problems.constraint: retrofit only: no change to the tower structure or fill packing; allowed measures: side-stream filtration with automatic backwash or in-duct UV irradiation on the recirculation loop only; continuous chemical biocide dosing is excluded; disinfection residual must stay below 0.2 mg/L free oxidant at the basin outlet
problems.question: What engineering change, intervention, or design would prevent or mitigate the stated failure under the stated constraint, and what concrete test would falsify the proposed approach?
user_variables: use only the two allowed measure classes
keep plant availability above 99 percent
sampling cadence stays monthly

problems.device: 10-inch carbon-steel subsea gas-production riser with water condensation at the dewpoint band, 1200 m water depth
problems.failure: top-of-line condensation corrosion thins the riser wall at the 8 o'clock section; ILI runs show 0.9 mm/year loss against a 3.2 mm wall, with a predicted through-wall date in 6 years
problems.constraint: allowed measures: batch corrosion-inhibitor injection at the riser inlet or in-line inspection pigging frequency increase only; no internal coating or lined spool re-placement is permitted because the line cannot be shut down; inhibitor concentration is capped at 25 ppm for environmental discharge limits
problems.question: What engineering change, intervention, or design would prevent or mitigate the stated failure under the stated constraint, and what concrete test would falsify the proposed approach?
user_variables: no shutdown or line break is permitted
injection points are limited to the existing umbilical
ILI tool access is every 18 months at most

problems.device: pharmacy-grade vaccine refrigerator bank (six 400 L cabinets) in a regional distribution hub, with 300 vials of mRNA product
problems.failure: defrost cycles and door-open recoveries let cabinet air exceed +8 C for 12-20 minutes about three times per week; two excursions per quarter ruin a shelf of product worth 40k
problems.constraint: procedure-and-controls only: allowed measures are controller setpoint and defrost-interval retuning, plus a door-discipline procedure with an audible alarm; no compressor, evaporator, or cabinet replacement is permitted; alarm delay after door closure must stay under 60 seconds so staff can restock
problems.question: What engineering change, intervention, or design would prevent or mitigate the stated failure under the stated constraint, and what concrete test would falsify the proposed approach?
user_variables: no hardware replacement is permitted
staff cannot add door-opening logging paperwork
the cabinets hold validated setpoint certificates

problems.device: paper-machine dryer section, 40 cylinders, with hood exhaust ducts and a lint accumulation history at the rope-return area
problems.failure: lint layers 3-8 mm thick build on duct bends and rope pulleys; a hot-bearing spark ignited duct lint last year, causing a 14-hour outage, and near-miss temperature excursions now occur monthly
problems.constraint: allowed measures: hood ventilation rebalancing and duct access-door cleaning procedure with IR surface-temperature monitoring only; replacement of dryer cans, ropes, or duct geometry is excluded; cleaning may only occur during the weekly 4-hour planned stop
problems.question: What engineering change, intervention, or design would prevent or mitigate the stated failure under the stated constraint, and what concrete test would falsify the proposed approach?
user_variables: no duct rerouting or can replacement
cleaning windows are the weekly 4-hour stop only
IR cameras already exist at six fixed points

problems.device: single-phase immersion-cooling tank (synthetic ester dielectric) hosting 38 GPU servers, 55 C bulk fluid, 1.2 m deep
problems.failure: fluid acid number rises 0.09 mgKOH/g per year and dissolved copper from server heatsinks darkens the fluid; dielectric breakdown margin has fallen from 55 kV to 41 kV against a 35 kV trip line
problems.constraint: allowed measures: side-loop fluid fine filtration with activated-alumina cartridges or scheduled partial top-up with fresh inhibitor-blended fluid only; full fluid replacement or a fluid-chemistry redesign is excluded this budget cycle; tank downtime may not exceed one 6-hour window per quarter
problems.question: What engineering change, intervention, or design would prevent or mitigate the stated failure under the stated constraint, and what concrete test would falsify the proposed approach?
user_variables: no full fluid replacement is permitted
downtime budget is one 6-hour window per quarter
cartridge housings already exist on the side loop

problems.device: drip-irrigation fertigation system over 2.4 hectares of greenhouse tomatoes, with 16 mm laterals and pressure-compensating emitters
problems.failure: calcium-phosphate precipitate and root fragments clog about 8 percent of emitters per season; outlet uniformity drops below 85 percent by week 14, stressing fruit quality; flushing crews recover only half the loss
problems.constraint: allowed measures: acid-dosing interval retuning (nitric acid, pH floor 5.6) and screen-filter flush automation only; emitter or lateral redesign is excluded; root-growth intrusion must be addressed by flushing procedure, not by chemicals above the stated pH floor
problems.question: What engineering change, intervention, or design would prevent or mitigate the stated failure under the stated constraint, and what concrete test would falsify the proposed approach?
user_variables: no emitter or lateral redesign
acid floor is pH 5.6 for root safety
the fertilizer recipe is fixed by contract

problems.device: traction elevator with a DC door operator and belt-driven door hanger rollers serving 60 openings/day per door
problems.failure: door hanger rollers flatten and the operator belt slips; the door stalls and the controller trips on door-timeout about once per month, trapping passengers between floors
problems.constraint: the controller already logs door-motor current per operation and door close-duration; the failure-DEFINING event is the door-timeout trip, so the predictor must trigger on the operator's measured current signature (the primary indicator); floor-vibration or cabin-acceleration sensors are not installed and must not be assumed
problems.question: Propose the most cost-effective measurable leading indicator (predictor) for the stated failure, its operating threshold, and the concrete test that would validate or kill the predictor.
user_variables: use only existing door-motor current and close-duration logs; warn >=14 days before a timeout trip; <=1 false alarm per 10 elevators/month

problems.device: centrifugal irrigation pump with a 2.4 km PVC main, check valve at the pump, and air valves at two high points
problems.failure: sudden power-off events send a return surge that fatigues the PVC main at glued joints; two joint bursts in three years each flooded a field for a day
problems.constraint: pressure transducers already log at 10 Hz at the pump header and at high point 2; the failure-DEFINING quantity is the peak pressure transient amplitude at the pump header (the primary indicator); soil or joint-strain instrumentation does not exist and must not be assumed
problems.question: Propose the most cost-effective measurable leading indicator (predictor) for the stated failure, its operating threshold, and the concrete test that would validate or kill the predictor.
user_variables: use only existing 10 Hz pressure traces; warn when cumulative surge dose approaches the joint fatigue budget; <=2 false alerts per season

problems.device: rotating-rack bakery oven with a rope door gasket and steam injection, 14 bakes/day
problems.failure: the door gasket hardens and shrinks; steam leaks at the door frame and the oven can no longer recover to setpoint between racks, so crust quality fails specification about twice a month
problems.constraint: the oven controller already records steam-valve duty and cavity-temperature recovery time per bake; the failure-DEFINING symptom is the cavity temperature-recovery time after rack loading (the primary indicator); door-frame IR imaging is not installed and must not be assumed
problems.question: Propose the most cost-effective measurable leading indicator (predictor) for the stated failure, its operating threshold, and the concrete test that would validate or kill the predictor.
user_variables: use only existing recovery-time and steam-duty logs; warn >=10 bakes before a quality failure; <=1 false alarm per 60 bakes

problems.device: warehouse fleet of 18 lead-acid forklift batteries on opportunity charging with a shared watering cart
problems.failure: opportunity charging drives electrolyte loss; cells watered late run low and sulfate on plate tops, and two batteries per year lose over 20 percent capacity and are retired early
problems.constraint: chargers already log charge amp-hours and end-of-charge voltage per battery, and the watering cart logs fills per battery; the failure-DEFINING quantity is the electrolyte level deficit the fills compensate (the primary indicator); single-cell impedance probes are not installed and must not be assumed
problems.question: Propose the most cost-effective measurable leading indicator (predictor) for the stated failure, its operating threshold, and the concrete test that would validate or kill the predictor.
user_variables: use only charger and watering-cart logs; warn >=7 days before a capacity-loss threshold crossing; <=1 false alarm per fleet per month

problems.device: air-cooled screw chiller rejecting heat for an MRI suite, with a variable-speed condenser fan bank and a fixed evaporator flow
problems.failure: at high ambient the chiller surges intermittently; a surge trip aborts the magnet's cooling interlock and cancels scans; four scan-session cancellations last quarter each cost 9k
problems.constraint: the chiller controller already logs suction pressure, discharge pressure, and condenser fan staging every 10 seconds; the failure-DEFINING precursor is the condenser approach temperature (the primary indicator); compressor vibration sensors are not installed and must not be assumed
problems.question: Propose the most cost-effective measurable leading indicator (predictor) for the stated failure, its operating threshold, and the concrete test that would validate or kill the predictor.
user_variables: use only existing 10 s pressure and fan-stage logs; warn >=20 minutes before a surge trip; <=1 false alarm per 30 cooling days

problems.device: asphalt paver with a vibratory screed plate set paving 1.5 km of arterial road per week
problems.failure: screed plate bottoms wear thin at the leading edge; mat thickness drifts 4 mm below target before crews notice, forcing a 200 m mill-and-repave correction twice a season
problems.constraint: the paver logs screed vibration frequency, amplitude, and extension-plate position per shift, and grade control logs mat thickness sensor readings per meter; the failure-DEFINING quantity is the mat thickness sensor deviation at constant screed settings (the primary indicator); plate-thickness ultrasonic probes are not installed and must not be assumed
problems.question: Propose the most cost-effective measurable leading indicator (predictor) for the stated failure, its operating threshold, and the concrete test that would validate or kill the predictor.
user_variables: use only existing paver and grade-control logs; warn >=150 m before a 4 mm drift correction; <=1 false alarm per 10 km
